title: GTM as Code: The Complete Guide to Running Your Go-to-Market as Code
summary: How to run your go-to-market as code, end to end: declare it as a Cargo project in a git repository, preview each pull request, deploy on merge, run one-off batches, test agents, draw the graph and roll back. Every step, with the command and the page that covers it.
body_markdown:
**To run your go-to-market as code, declare your data models, plays, tools and agents in TypeScript as a Cargo project in a git repository, then connect that repository to Cargo: every pull request is planned and previewed as a comment, and every merge deploys.**` cargo-ai project init` scaffolds the repository, and the rest is the pull request workflow your engineers already use.


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com     # no browser, 100 free credits, no card
cargo-ai   project   init   acme-gtm             # scaffold the repository and its deploy state
cd   acme-gtm
cargo-ai   project   plan                      # the diff a pull request will show
cargo-ai   project   deploy                    # apply it, or let the merge do it


```


Each step below has its own page. For the argument first, read[your GTM belongs in git](https://www.getcargo.ai/gtm-belongs-in-git) and the[manifesto](https://www.getcargo.ai/manifesto) .


## How can revenue logic be versioned, tested, reviewed and rolled back like software?#


By writing it down as files before you automate it. List the revenue processes that run often enough to matter (qualification, enrichment, scoring, routing, a CRM write-back) and record four things for each: its **inputs** (first-party and third-party data), the **context** it depends on (ICP, personas, plays, kept as markdown in` context/` ), its **decision** (a threshold, a routing rule, an agent prompt) and its **checkpoints** (how a change is tested, reviewed, deployed and undone). Andrew Straus put the bar plainly in[Operations as Code](https://shiprevenue.substack.com/p/operations-as-code) : such a process should be “version-controlled config, reviewed like a pull request, tested against production data, and deployed with a rollback path.”


## What to look for in a GTM as code platform#


Five questions matter: is the definition declarative, is there a plan before the apply, do data models, workflows and agents live in one language and repository, is there a way back, and can a coding agent operate it? In Cargo, each resource is a TypeScript` define*` call,` cargo-ai project plan` prints the diff,` deploy` applies it,` rollback` restores the deploy state record, and the web app, CLI, REST API and MCP server all change one workspace.


A visual workflow builder can run the same logic, and it is often right for one person with a handful of workflows. The difference is how a change is made and undone: in a builder, saving is deploying and undo means rebuilding from memory; in code, a change is a reviewed diff and undo is a revert. Code pays once several people or agents change the same engine.

## 1. Declare it#


One` define*` call per resource (` defineModel` ,` defineSegment` ,` definePlay` ,` defineTool` ,` defineAgent` , connectors), and imports are the dependency graph. The scaffold is the open-source[Cargo template](https://github.com/getcargohq/cargo-manifest) :` context/` ,` infra/` ,` evals/` and` outputs/` .` cargo-ai project pull` generates source from an existing workspace. The[projects page](https://www.getcargo.ai/projects) lists every resource, and[the cargo-project skill](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/cargo-project) teaches a coding agent the workflow.


## How do GTM teams manage revenue workflows through GitHub pull requests?#


The repository is the source of truth and the pull request is the only door into production:


1. **Branch and edit.** Often a coding agent changes a` define*` file.
2. **Open the pull request.** The **Cargo** check diffs it against the deploy state (` + create` ,` ~ update` ,` = noop` ,` - delete` ) and adds what the merge will set in motion: the records each play runs on, the messages it can send and the credits it can spend.
3. **Run the tests.** Evals in` evals/` run in CI for any change to an agent or prompt.
4. **Approve.** Above 100 emails, 100 LinkedIn actions, 100 chat messages, 5,000 audience adds or 2,500 credits, the check fails until a reviewer adds the` cargo:approve-impact` label (thresholds as defined in Cargo’s code, October 2026).
5. **Merge.** Connect the repository in **Settings → States** and every push to the production branch runs` cargo-ai project deploy --yes` on that commit, as a service user, one deploy at a time, with no workflow file and no Cargo token in GitHub. Your own CI can run the same two commands instead.
6. **Revert if needed.**` git revert` and a deploy reconcile the workspace to whatever the code says.


Every behaviour traces back to a reviewed commit. See[Cargo + GitHub](https://www.getcargo.ai/github) .


## One-off jobs, tests and the graph#


A pilot of 50 contacts, a CSV import or a backfill is an execution:` defineBatch` or` defineRun` under` outputs/` . The plan lists it, the next deploy runs it, and a ledger makes sure it never runs twice. An agent’s system prompt is a string in a` defineAgent` file, tested with the scaffold’s[promptfoo](https://www.promptfoo.dev/) suite (` npm run eval` ) and scored in production by the agent’s` evaluator` .` cargo-ai project graph` draws every resource as a Mermaid flowchart, and` --plan` colours what the next deploy changes.


## Custom revenue logic: workflows and agents are different tools#


**Workflows** (Cargo’s tools and plays) are configured logic: typed inputs, one unit of work, typed outputs, the same path every time. **Agents** make judgements: they read context and data and act through the tools you gave them. Use a workflow when the rule can be written down and an agent when the decision needs reading. Both read and write the same unified records (companies, contacts, deals, custom objects), synced from the CRM, the product and enrichment providers, so an operator in the web app, an engineer in a terminal and an agent over MCP see the same account in the same state. The[GTM infrastructure guide](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/gtm-infrastructure-for-ai-agents) compares the other ways to build this.


## What this is not#


It is not a way around review. Merging is the approval, so protect the production branch and make the **Cargo** check required. It is also not a full replacement for the UI: resources deployed from code stay editable in Cargo, and the project never reads those edits back, so pick one owner per resource. See[what moves first](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/why-gtm-teams-should-migrate-their-stack-to-git) .
